segments.t: Following his bizarre breakdown on the movie set, Jean Dujardin feels deep remorse about costing ASK a major commission. But Andrea arrives with empathy and understanding to comfort her star client. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Je t'ai causé beaucoup d'ennuis.
Tu as surtout mordu ce chien!
Tout le monde en parle déjà?
Tout Paris adore cette folle histoire!
Je te fais perdre ton argent.
Je suis vraiment désolé pour toi.
Non Jean, c'est moi la responsable.
Pourquoi dis-tu une chose pareille?
J'ai pensé aux affaires avant tout.
Je n'ai pas assez pensé à toi.
Ce rôle était trop difficile pour toi.
Ce personnage m'a complètement transformé.
J'aurais dû mieux te protéger, Jean.
Merci Andréa, tu es une vraie amie.
Let's examine how Andrea and Jean reconcile step by step.
Je t'ai causé beaucoup d'ennuis.
'I caused you a lot of trouble.' Jean expresses remorse for his disruptive behavior on set. Notice how 'have' leads directly into the noun meaning 'troubles'.
Tu as surtout mordu ce chien!
'You mostly bit that dog!' Andrea brings up the most bizarre incident with irony. The informal 'you' form around 'have' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Tout le monde en parle déjà?
'Is everyone already talking about it?' Jean wonders about the public reaction in Paris. The verb meaning 'is talking' pairs naturally with the noun for 'world' in everyday conversation.
Tout Paris adore cette folle histoire!
'All of Paris loves this crazy story!' Andrea assures him that the industry finds it hilarious. Dropping the subject pronoun turns the verb for 'adores' into a direct, punchy command.
Je te fais perdre ton argent.
'I make you lose your money.' Jean worries about the heavy financial fallout for his agent. The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'make', turning the action back onto the subject.
Je suis vraiment désolé pour toi.
'I am really sorry for you.' Jean apologizes sincerely to his devoted representative. The descriptive adjective for 'sorry' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Non Jean, c'est moi la responsable.
'No Jean, I am the one responsible.' Andrea refuses to let him shoulder all the blame. The key noun here means 'one responsible', anchored by its matching French article.
Pourquoi dis-tu une chose pareille?
'Why do you say such a thing?' Jean is surprised by her generous and self-critical attitude. Inverting the verb and pronoun around 'do you say' creates a crisp, polished question.
J'ai pensé aux affaires avant tout.
'I thought about business above all.' Andrea admits she focused excessively on contracts. The verb meaning 'have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'business' in everyday conversation.
Je n'ai pas assez pensé à toi.
'I did not think enough about you.' Andrea regrets neglecting the human emotional toll on her actor. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'thought'.
Ce rôle était trop difficile pour toi.
'This role was too difficult for you.' Andrea recognizes how deeply the extreme part affected him. Notice how 'was' leads directly into the noun meaning 'role'.
Ce personnage m'a complètement transformé.
'This character completely transformed me.' Jean explains how lost he felt inside the role. The verb meaning 'has' pairs naturally with the noun for 'character' in everyday conversation.
J'aurais dû mieux te protéger, Jean.

'I should have protected you better, Jean.' Andrea acknowledges her protective duty as an agent. The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'would have', turning the action back onto the subject.
Merci Andréa, tu es une vraie amie.

'Thank you Andrea, you are a true friend.' Jean deeply appreciates her understanding and support. The adjective meaning 'true' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes. Now let's listen to the scene once more from start to finish.

Merci Andréa, tu es une vraie amie.
That's it for this scene around andrea's comfort. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'caused' and 'troubles'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
